'''Scipio''' was an [[Water/Legends|ice]]- and snow-covered [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Albarrio sector/Legends|Albarrio sector]]. An important world for the [[Muun/Legends|Muuns]] and the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]], the world had frozen peaks dotted with towering columns and graceful arches.

==History==
The planet was at some point host to a warrior culture, whose influence could still be seen in the inhabitants' clothing styles which mimicked armor. The people also used tattoos to indicate status.<ref name="TCWCE">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

It was an important world of the [[Muun/Legends|Muun]] species and [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]].<ref name="OldFriend" /> Using the resources of [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]] to back the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Galactic Credit Standard]], the Banking Clan became important for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], as it utilized the credit as a galactic currency. The Clan built its massive vaults on Scipio, where the bank profits were safely held. Other outside agencies, power brokers, and representatives of various cartels made their home on Scipio, hoping to ensure their place in the galactic market.<ref name="EV" />

[[File:Scipio.png|thumb|left|180px|A settlement on Scipio, a stronghold of the InterGalactic Banking Clan]]

[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Rush Clovis/Legends|Rush Clovis]] represented the Banking Clan from [[25 BBY/Legends|25]] to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] until he was arrested by fellow senator [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]] on [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]]. In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], Rush Clovis became the head of the Banking Clan conglomerate, after the Council of Five was arrested for corruption and fraud. To prevent the Banking clan from becoming corrupt again, both the Galactic Republic and the Separatists agreed to send ambassadors to the planet, to secure both parties' agendas. [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] was sent to represent the Galactic Republic and [[Bec Lawise/Legends|Bec Lawise]] was sent on the behalf of the Confederacy. Clovis' appointment as the head of the InterGalactic Banking Clan did not last long, as he was killed during the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] attack on the planet, sacrificing himself to save Amidala. The [[Clone Commander/Legends|clone trooper commander]] [[Thorn/Legends|Thorn]] perished on this planet in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] 20 BBY during the attack and short occupation by the Confederacy.

When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] came to power at the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Scipio was subjugated, though the [[Core Five/Legends|Core Five]] were allowed to maintain their positions. [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Boyse/Legends|Boyse]] commanded the blockade of the planet from aboard his flagship the ''[[Exchequer/Legends|Exchequer]]'', ensuring that the Core Five maintained their loyalty to His Imperial Majesty. Despite this, the Imperial control was secretly being thwarted by Muuns and others working on the world. Using secret tunnels below the main vault, some agents of rebellion used vaults hidden in [[Frigia Canyons]] to move untraceable credits around.<ref name="EV" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Thorgeld-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|250px|In ''The Essential Atlas'', Scipio was identified as a world in the Core]]
Scipio was first referenced in "[[Senate Spy]]," an episode of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''.<ref name="SS" /> The [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', published in [[2008]], originally placed the planet in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> According to [[Jason Fry]], co-author of the book, the decision to place the planet in the Core was made when the only known information about Scipio was that it was the homeworld of Rush Clovis, so the authors felt that the Core was a fitting choice. However, once ''The Clone Wars'' went into more detail about Scipio, including how it was an important world to the InterGalactic Banking Clan, the planet was moved to the Outer Rim Territories near [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]] as it made more sense to have it within the geographic Banking Clan sphere.<ref name="Jason Fry Cite">{{JCFCite|url=posts/53103573|board=Literature|thread=Wookieepedia, the Star Wars wiki|user=jasonfry|date=2016-01-08|time=2:05 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220103244/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/wookieepedia-the-star-wars-wiki.20673016/page-111|quote=To better fit the storytelling. Scipio was placed in the Core when nothing was known about it other than that it was the homeworld of Rush Clovis. A Core placement seemed to fit based on that, though it wasn't much to go on. When Clone Wars gave us stories actually set on Scipio, we saw that it was a critical IGBC world with a significant Muun presence, so it was moved to a location in the ORT near Muunilinst. Which makes *far*more sense than the Core.|archivefile=File:Jason Fry on Scipios location.png}}</ref> Nevertheless, the reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' placed Scipio in the Core.<ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> The [[Fantasy Flight Games]] roleplaying sourcebook ''[[Endless Vigil]]'' breaks with the majority of [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] sources by claiming Scipio is the Muun homeworld.<ref name="EV" />
